title: Pareto-optimal work extraction and the thermodynamic cost of precision in quantum information engines
summary: We study a finite-time quantum information engine in which a two-level system is measured by a quantum harmonic oscillator acting as a meter and where useful work is extracted conditionally on the measurement outcome. Using multi-objective optimisation, we find a Pareto-optimal trade-off between extractable work and its fluctuations and show that reducing fluctuations entails higher thermodynamic costs: greater information consumption, more engine cycles, longer operation time, and reduced average work output.
